headline: Nikkei 225 Falls as Stronger Yen From Rare Joint US-Japan Currency Intervention Hits Exporter Shares
summary: Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 0.94% after a rare coordinated US-Japan currency intervention strengthened the yen. Exporter shares were hit, and the move is the first coordinated intervention in decades.
why: The Nikkei 225 is Japan's benchmark index of large listed companies, many of which earn significant revenue overseas and are sensitive to yen strength.

impacts.name: Nikkei 225
impacts.why: Exporter shares fell as the stronger yen reduces the yen value of overseas earnings.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: A rare joint US-Japan currency intervention strengthened the yen, which weighed on export-dependent manufacturers in the index.
